column1: # clues.tsv for ft_atoi — pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".

How do you turn a run of digit characters into the integer they spell? What does a digit's place in the run say about how much it is worth? A digit character is not the numeric value it stands for: what separates the two? And what should an input with no digits at all give?
Before any digits there can be blank bytes to skip. Which characters count as whitespace here, beyond a plain space? Are you skipping every one of them, and only at the very start?

After the whitespace can come a run of '+' and '-' signs. What does the subject say decides the sign of the result when there are several? Read that sentence again and check each case below against it. What does a sign with no digit after it produce?
Reading the digits has to stop somewhere. The moment you meet a byte that is not a digit, what should happen to everything after it?
